note: Known verdicts for past renders and reference screenshots. calibrate.py must reproduce every label before the judge is trusted. music-content-color.png is the owner's supplied music-app collage: its now-playing screen pairs a full-screen burgundy palette with visible pink album art. It tests visual coherence, not proof of token usage or color extraction. The adaptive-* labels list four frames each (light phone, foldable, tablet, desktop) because R-adaptive compares size classes: the music set only rearranges the phone layout (fail); the settings and trek sets reveal a second pane or more content (pass). The text-* labels test R-text: the trek and finance phone renders have scrolling content partly under a floating toolbar or FAB (pass, Google allows it); the music collision render draws a subtitle over the title (fail). finance-v3-neon passes R-surfaces: its mint backdrop, hero card, and category tiles are one full-screen content-color treatment with tonal steps, which the rubric allows. The wear-* images are the main-watch and main-watch-large renders of wear-src/<name>.proposal.json, so they can be rendered again; the older images have no committed sources. good-player labels no R-wear-round verdict: its full-width volume slider meets the round edge, which is a judgment call. The code-* labels test the code items, which the judge grades from the proposal source: each names its `.explore.kt` in `source` beside its light render. code-settings-good passes all four (fields and blur pass because it has none); code-settings-bad leaves section titles without heading(), keeps each control's own callback with no toggleable or selectable row, and fades the summary time row to alpha 0; code-recipes-bad uses the value-based search field and puts white text over an image that only blur softens; code-recipes-good fixes both with rememberTextFieldState and a tonal surface behind the text. The code-signin set is a saved-recipes screen with a search bar, a blurred hero whose text sits on a tonal surface, and an email and password form. All three pass R-blur, because blur there is a backdrop and the surface keeps the text readable. code-signin-good uses the search bar's textFieldState input field, a state-based email field, and OutlinedSecureTextField. Each bad file breaks exactly one R-fields rule, so a judge that skips that rule misses its label: code-signin-bad masks the password with PasswordVisualTransformation, and code-signin-search-bad holds the search query in a plain String.
